quote.translation: The reason such acts are deemed unlawful is that, whereas the gain and loss of property ought in general to have a proper cause, taking a mere chance circumstance as that cause runs counter to the idea of justice in economic society" (Ono Seiichirō, Lectures on Criminal Law, p. 460).

regions.text: 経落的意志活動の目的々必然性に對して賭博および富籤が目前々横極釣個然を構成する限りに於て、国民羅済の機能を害する。のとして法律が禁するのである。

quote.translation: It is insofar as gambling and lotteries constitute a positive teleological contingency with respect to the teleological necessity of economic activity of will that the law forbids them, as harmful to the functioning of the national economy.

regions.text: 「偶然の轍慮の概念は後に説く離接的偶然の概念によつて初めて根源約理解を可能にされるのであるが（第三率第入都参照）法律の開心の傾域にあつては目的々積極的偶然の機念を以て足ると云っても差支へないのである。

quote.translation: The concept of "chance winning or losing" can be understood at its root only through the concept of disjunctive contingency, which I discuss later (see Chapter 3, section 8), but within the domain of the law's concern we may safely say that the concept of positive teleological contingency suffices.

regions.text: 要するに、目々積極偶然は法律上にいふ偶然の騒する次元であり、その「目的なき目的」によつて「故意」2外見接近に置かれることがぁ

quote.translation: Positive teleological contingency, in short, is the dimension to which chance in the legal sense belongs, and through its "purpose without purpose" it is sometimes brought into an outward proximity with "intention".

regions.text: 「目約なき目餡」の葉介によって、目時々積極的偶然が「故意と舞別し難い様態をさへ取り待ることを述べた。アリストテレスの「アウトマトン

quote.translation: We have seen that, through the mediation of "purpose without purpose", positive teleological contingency can take on a form so close to "intention" that the two are hard to tell apart.

regions.text: 」（airoparor）と「ラュク」（さx）との皿別もこの點から理解することができる。

quote.translation: It is from this point that Aristotle's distinction between automaton (αὐτόματον) and tychē (τύχη) can also be understood.
